findings.title: Embed template has invalid ERB (`end if`)
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` compiles to the Ruby statement `end if`, which is a SyntaxError. Rendering `/embed/best` when a topic already exists (the success path in EmbedController#best) will raise while compiling the template, so the iframe never shows highlights. It must be `<% end %>`.

findings.title: raw_html cook path stores and serves unsanitized HTML
findings.body: Post#cook returns `raw` unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, skipping PrettyText and Discourse's sanitizer. TopicEmbed.import persists RSS/Readability HTML with that cook method, and the embed view prints it with `raw post.cooked` (the main topic UI also treats cooked as HTML). PollFeed does `CGI.unescapeHTML` on feed content first, so entity-encoded markup becomes live tags, and Readability's allow-list still permits `javascript:`/`data:` href and src. Any feed item or fetched page can therefore plant stored XSS that runs for every forum visitor, not just inside the embed iframe. The imported-from footer makes this worse by interpolating the URL into an href with no escaping (`<a href='#{url}'>` in TopicEmbed.import), so a quote in an otherwise allowed http(s) URL breaks out of the attribute.

findings.title: Unauthenticated embed URL fetch is an SSRF and topic-spam vector
findings.body: import_remote uses `open(url).read` (open-uri) with no timeout, size limit, or redirect restriction. EmbedController#best is a public GET whose only gate is `URI(request.referer).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. Referer is client-controlled, so any caller can spoof it and pass `embed_url` on the configured host. TopicRetriever then fetches that URL; open-uri follows redirects to arbitrary hosts (including link-local and cloud metadata). Each miss also enqueues RetrieveTopic with no controller-side dedupe, so unique URLs create unbounded jobs and, on success, topics posted as embed_by_username. open-uri is not even required from this file, so the fetch only works if some other file has already patched Kernel#open.

findings.title: Feed poll crashes unless every item has string content
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every SimpleRSS item has a String `content`. RSS 2.0 items typically expose `description` and leave `content` nil; Atom can also omit it. Nil (or a non-string) raises NoMethodError, and because there is no rescue the hourly job aborts before later items are imported. `String#scrub` is also Ruby 2.1+ only, so this line fails on Ruby 2.0 even when content is present. Use description/content fallback and guard nil before unescaping.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is the full referer, so resize is dropped
findings.body: The embed layout calls `parent.postMessage(..., request.referer)`. postMessage's targetOrigin must be an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`), not a full URL with path and query. Browsers drop the message (or throw) when it does not match the parent origin. embed.js also sets the iframe to `scrolling=no` and only grows it on `discourse-resize`, so the comments frame stays at the default height and clips the discussion. Pass the referer origin only (and escape it for the JS string).

findings.title: Resize listener accepts any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl
findings.body: The check is `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, i.e. accept when the sender origin is any substring of discourseUrl, not when it equals the forum origin. A shorter origin that is a prefix matches: if discourseUrl is `https://discuss.example.com`, a window at `https://discuss.example.co` has index 0 and is accepted. That page can postMessage a `discourse-resize` and set the iframe height arbitrarily (hide comments or stretch the frame over the host page). Compare parsed origins for equality, and require index 0 only if a prefix check is kept.

findings.title: Embed controller spec expects a sync retrieve the action does not do
findings.body: The 'no previous embed' example expects `TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve` during `get :best`. EmbedController#best only calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`, so mocha fails this example and the job/throttle path is untested. The other success example renders `embed/best`, which currently raises SyntaxError on `end if`, so the `response.should be_success` after-hook fails as well. The spec will not pass as written and does not lock in the async behavior.

findings.title: Disqus import drops category, original date, and offline permalinks
findings.body: The importer no longer accepts `--category` and no longer passes `created_at` or `category` into topic creation. It now depends on `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which HTTP-fetches `t[:link]` and returns nil on any network/HTTP error. The following comment import is skipped entirely when that fetch fails, so a dead or blocked article URL drops the whole Disqus thread instead of creating the previous permalink stub. Category placement and original thread timestamps are also lost, and a single failed fetch aborts the rest of the file because nothing rescues `open`.

findings.title: embed_url is varchar(255) but used as the unique lookup key
findings.body: `t.string :embed_url` is a 255-character varchar, with a unique index on that column. TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed and import look up the full URL. Article and RSS links with tracking query strings routinely exceed 255 characters, so insert raises and the topic is never associated; truncated values would also collide or miss on lookup. Store embed_url as text (and index a hash if a unique constraint is still required).

findings.title: content_sha1 is advanced even when the post is not updated
findings.body: On change, import always calls `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` after `revise!`, without checking that revise!/save succeeded. PostRevisor#revise! returns false when raw is unchanged and still returns true if `save` fails; either way the SHA is overwritten. The next poll then treats the feed item as already imported and never retries, so the topic body stays stale. If the linked post was deleted, `embed.post` is nil and `PostRevisor.new(post)` raises, which aborts the rest of the feed run. Update the SHA only after a successful save, and skip or recreate when the post is gone.
